_note: Skeleton for docs/close-board-exemptions.json — the factory data file read by tests/test_close_board_recorded.py. Copy it into docs/ (the example itself is never read) and add an entry ONLY when a post-invariant `close` row omitted `board=closed` and NO TRUTHFUL VALUE RESTORES ITS TOKEN. That is the bar, and it is a TRUTHFULNESS bar, never a claim of unreachability: `tools/ledger.py repair --invariant close_board_recorded --append-detail board=closed` DOES reach a pushed row and returns rc=0, so 'the repair space is empty' is FALSE as a ground and is UNEXPRESSIBLE here (the `bar` key below admits no such value). The ground that holds is the gate's own token — 'the board state the settling lane recorded AT CLOSE TIME' — measured against the row's own `ts`: if the board close happened AFTER the row was written, a `board=closed` appended today asserts a state that did not hold at the row's own instant, which is the no-backfill family (docs/instruments/ledger.md line 1048) — a falsified record, not a repair. That is the 'a gate whose only exits are barred is a stop with no andon cord' class only in its TRUTHFUL form: the row is reachable, and the one value that would satisfy the gate would be false. `bar` is a DECLARATION KEY WITH ONE LAWFUL VALUE on this surface, `no-truthful-value` (docs/instruments/ledger.md §9.12): the loader REQUIRES it and refuses every other value, so the falsified ground cannot be re-stated as data. A claim of ABSENCE is a MECHANICAL claim, so an entry's `reason` must carry the RECORDED PROBE of the attempt — the command, its rc, and the effect read back (docs/instruments/ledger.md §9.3) — or the claim is not stated. Key every entry by the row's own `n` — the value the gate reads — so a FUTURE close (a different `n`) can never be excused by it; a short or invented key matches nothing while looking like it should. `reason` and `proof` are both REQUIRED, and the proof must be the external receipt that the board close ACTUALLY HAPPENED (e.g. `gh issue view <N> --json state,closedAt` reading CLOSED) — an exemption states that the close was not RECORDED, never that it did not happen. `domain` must be the declared value 'the board close happened but was not recorded in the row'. It is printed as an 'excused:' line with its reason and proof on EVERY gate run, so it is a visible debt rather than forgiveness, and the closing line distinguishes clean from excused. A malformed entry, or one that matches NO violation, is a gate ERROR rather than a silent pass. Expect this list to stay near-empty: one entry is a debt, and a SECOND is a process defect — the remedy for a second is a mechanism that stops the omission at the write path, never a third row. THAT MECHANISM NOW SHIPS: `tools/ledger.py append` REFUSES a `close` row whose canonical trailer declares no `board=closed`, reading the token through `declared_board_closed` in `tools/field_predicate.py` — the same home this gate's own token is composed from, so the refuser and the detector cannot drift. A fourth of this shape therefore cannot be written at all; the entries in this file are history that no truthful repair value reaches, and are the debt the mechanism retires.
